title: Dastane Se Phone Kyun Nahi Chalta?

lines.text: ایسی باتوں کے لیے، فالو کریں۔
lines.spoken: ایسی باتوں کے لیے، فالو کریں۔

fact_notes: Phone screens use projected capacitive touch: a grid of transparent electrodes (row and column lines, usually ITO) under the glass carries a small changing signal.
A bare finger is conductive and forms a capacitor with the electrodes, drawing away part of the field; the controller sees capacitance drop at that row/column crossing.
Touch controllers scan the grid many times a second; modern phones report touch sampling rates of roughly 120-240 Hz, so 'more than a hundred times a second' is safe.
Ordinary gloves are insulating and keep the finger too far from the glass to change the capacitance, so no touch registers (touchscreen gloves add conductive thread).
